items.title: Warren Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995
items.q: I’ve been listening to you know those Beiderbecke records since I was a kid. I knew most of the stuff from having played it millions of times

ctx.x: Did you do a lot of listening before that, or was it already a part of you?

I don’t — I mean I’ve been listening to you know those Beiderbecke records since I was a kid. I knew most of the stuff from having played it millions of times, just as I knew a lot of Louis Armstrong solos from having played it a hundred and — you know, a little kid with a trumpet and you hear somebody do something like “West End Blues” — it’s still pretty astounding. Even now, I’ve played the trumpet for forty years, and every time I hear “West End Blues” I think it’s astounding. So yeah, I was prepared that…
He was an interesting character I guess, from what I read.
